reason: The hinge pins look useful for joining the dragon’s moving cut-out parts.
expectation: The pins will attach the wings to the body so they can move.

effect: The pins joined the cut-outs into a jointed dragon; it still needs a connection to the lifter.
reaction: The hinged dragon is a satisfying first piece.
reason: The jointed wing rods appear to connect the dragon's wings to the mechanism.
expectation: The rods will attach to the dragon's wings so the mechanism can move them.

effect: The wing rods cannot currently be combined with anything, so the dragon may need to be mounted first.
reaction: That was an unexpected ordering constraint.
reason: The jointed dragon likely needs to sit on the cam lifter before its wings can be connected.
expectation: The dragon will be mounted on the mechanism.

alternatives.reason: I could check its available partners first.

effect: The dragon is mounted, so the wing rods may now connect it to the lifter.
reaction: The mounting order makes more sense now.
reason: The rods should link the mounted wings to the moving mechanism.
expectation: The rods will connect the wings to the follower so they can wave.

effect: The rods now link the follower to both wings, with independent pivots at the wing roots.
reaction: It is satisfying to see how one rising follower can move both wings.
reason: The chapter asks for a wave with the original cam first, so the crank handle should let me test it.
expectation: Turning the handle will make the dragon wave using the original cam.

effect: The original cam produces one wing rise and fall per turn; the next step is to exchange it for the greeting cam.
reaction: The single wave makes the cam’s effect clear, and the old fair drawing is intriguing.
reason: The chapter calls for exchanging cams after the first wave, and the two-humped cam is the available replacement.
expectation: The greeting cam will replace the original cam so I can compare the dragon’s wave.

effect: The replacement cam is installed securely, with two rises ready to compare against the original cam.
reaction: The keeper pin and shaft-removal sequence makes the exchange feel mechanically concrete.
reason: The handle should let me test the new cam and compare its greeting with the first wave.
expectation: One turn will produce two rises and falls of the wings.

effect: The comparison is complete: the two-humped cam gives the dragon a double wave, and the fair has its waving dragon.
reaction: The wave-wave pattern is a satisfying payoff for changing the cam.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the wing rods was worthwhile because it showed how one follower moves two independently pivoting wings.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the rods before mounting the dragon was the least worthwhile moment; the ordering constraint was not apparent beforehand.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the rods could not be attached until the dragon was mounted.

arbitrary.text: The initial attachment order felt a little arbitrary at first, although mounting the body before connecting the rods made more sense afterward.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose to continue: comparing the cams made the mechanism understandable, and the old drawing raises an interesting question about the fair.
